demo-pilot-v1-systems.label: Primary keys
demo-pilot-v1-systems.excerpt: A primary key uniquely identifies a row and cannot contain null values.

demo-pilot-v1-systems.label: Foreign keys
demo-pilot-v1-systems.excerpt: A foreign key constrains references to a key in another table. A foreign key does not by itself make its column unique; many rows can reference the same parent.

demo-pilot-v1-systems.label: Inner joins
demo-pilot-v1-systems.excerpt: Joining Members to Teams on matching team_id produces three rows: Ari–Cedar, Bo–Cedar, Cam–Maple.

demo-pilot-v1-security.label: Server-side sessions
demo-pilot-v1-security.excerpt: After authentication, a session cookie can identify a server-side session. The server must check session validity and authorization on protected requests.

demo-pilot-v1-security.label: HttpOnly cookies
demo-pilot-v1-security.excerpt: HttpOnly prevents JavaScript from reading the cookie through document.cookie; it does not prevent every action an injected script could perform.

demo-pilot-v1-security.label: CSRF defenses
demo-pilot-v1-security.excerpt: A browser can automatically attach cookies to requests. This is why cookie authentication alone is not a complete CSRF defense. In the course example, state-changing requests require a permitted Origin; token-based defenses are another approach outside this example's implementation scope.
